key_insight: Changing the weight factors in Park’s two-temperature control temperature can noticeably alter hypersonic reentry flow predictions, especially for FIRE II, by shifting temperature, composition, and heat-flux distributions near the shock/stagnation region.
engineering_relevance: For hypersonic vehicle design and thermal protection, the choice of non-equilibrium model weights can materially affect predicted heating and near-wall flow behavior, so model calibration matters.
method: Solve reacting Navier–Stokes equations for thermochemical non-equilibrium hypersonic flow.
Compare Park’s two-temperature model using different weight-factor sets to define the control temperature.
Evaluate FIRE II (Earth, 11-species) and Mars Pathfinder (Mars, 8-species) cases along the stagnation streamline and at the stagnation-point heat flux.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparative numerical results showing strong sensitivity of FIRE II predictions to weight-factor choice, while Mars Pathfinder shows only minor changes, across Mach number, temperature modes, species mass fractions, and convective heat flux.
watch_item: The impact of the weight factors appears case-dependent, so conclusions may not transfer directly between Earth-entry and Mars-entry conditions without revalidation.
paper_title: Influence of Park's Two-Temperature Model Control Temperature on the Flow Properties in Hypersonic Reentry Conditions
